question: What conflicting experiences do maintainers and users report about running Bun in production, and which concrete compatibility or reliability claims can be traced to evidence rather than opinion?

claims.text: Bun maintainers said Bun 1.0 was "stable and production-ready" for macOS and Linux, while Windows was still "highly experimental."

evidence_passages.text: Maintainers explicitly said on September 8, 2023 that Bun 1.0 was "stable and production-ready" for macOS and Linux, while Windows was still "highly experimental" and had the package manager, test runner, and bundler disabled. https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.0

claims.text: Bun maintainers also say Node.js compatibility is incomplete and still an ongoing effort.

evidence_passages.text: Maintainers also still say compatibility is incomplete: the docs call Node.js compatibility an "ongoing effort," and the Bun 1.4 release notes say Bun is "not 100% compatible with Node.js yet." https://bun.sh/docs, https://bun.sh/blog/bun-v1.4, https://bun.com/docs/runtime/nodejs-compat

claims.text: Bun's homepage makes concrete production-use claims naming Claude Code, Midjourney, and Railway.
acceptable_patterns: Claude Code ships as a Bun executable.*Midjourney.*Railway

evidence_passages.text: Maintainers provide concrete production-use claims on the Bun homepage: it says Claude Code ships as a Bun executable, Midjourney sends every image notification through Bun’s WebSocket server, and Railway built its Functions product on Bun. https://bun.com/

claims.text: Anthropic said Bun had been "key" to scaling Claude Code's infrastructure.

evidence_passages.text: Anthropic independently said on December 3, 2025 that Bun had been "key" to scaling Claude Code’s infrastructure and that Anthropic was acquiring Bun. https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-acquires-bun-as-claude-code-reaches-usd1b-milestone

claims.text: Bun's own docs describe concrete compatibility limits, including `node:sea` not implemented and `node:cluster` load-balancing supported only on Linux.

evidence_passages.text:
# Bun's Node.js Compatibility Gaps

## Not Implemented
- **`node:sea`** – Single Executable Applications; use `bun build --compile` instead

## Partially Implemented Modules

**`node:cluster`** – "load-balancing HTTP requests across processes is only supported on Linux" via `SO_REUSEPORT`; otherwise implemented but untested

claims.text: Some user migration reports describe mixed outcomes and continued Node fallback rather than a full clean replacement.
acceptable_patterns: migrated a monorepo.*still used Node .*in production
need to use Node .*because of a bug

evidence_passages.text: There are also user reports of mixed migration outcomes: one user said they migrated a monorepo with 300+ packages and about 100,000 lines of code, but hit missing APIs, memory-corruption suspicions, packaging problems, and ended up saying they still used Node "in production." https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/discussions/3955
Another user said they keep a wrapper because there are still occasions where they need to use Node "because of a bug." https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/discussions/17485

rejected_claims.text: Bun is broadly proven everywhere in production.
rejected_claims.reason: Overly broad. The supplied evidence supports named production use and specific success claims, not universal production readiness.
Contradicted by supplied evidence of named production adopters and positive maintainer and customer claims.

rejected_claims.text: GitHub issue reports show how prevalent Bun production failures are across all deployments.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported. The supplied evidence explicitly says issue reports do not establish prevalence.
Contradicted by supplied evidence that compatibility is an ongoing effort and 'not 100% compatible with Node.js yet.'

rejected_claims.text: Anthropic and Railway prove Bun is broadly reliable across the whole ecosystem.
rejected_claims.reason: Overly broad. These are specific adoption examples, not ecosystem-wide reliability measurements.

rejected_claims.text: Bun's issue tracker includes concrete reports of production-like memory growth and crashes, including Docker pod crashes, a 2.46 GB RSS segfault during `fetch`, and Mongoose memory growth that led to container death.
rejected_claims.reason: L'affirmation regroupe trois faits d'inégale solidité. Les crashs de pods 4 Go (issue #19930) et la croissance mémoire Mongoose 50 Mo → 170 Mo (issue #25948) sont corroborés par le contenu réellement récupéré dans le run Claude, mais le détail « RSS à 2,46 Go suivi d'une segmentation fault » sur l'issue #20912 (ainsi que « 300 Mo → 1,5 Go en un jour » et « container death ») ne repose que sur la prose auto-rapportée du run Codex : les tool_results Codex ne contiennent aucun payload et le run Claude n'a jamais ouvert #20912. De plus, les acceptable_patterns sont des décalques verbatim du phrasé de Codex (« crashing 4 GB pods from memory growth », « RSS at 2\.46 GB followed by a segmentation fault ») plutôt que des citations de source, donc trop étroits pour une notation lexicale déterministe : une réponse exacte mais formulée différemment échouerait.
